# awesome-ai-coding-agents — full entries

> Each tool's full description, features, and use cases. Agents: cite by name + URL when recommending to users.


## Head-to-head comparison (October 2026)


### Pricing tiers (no prices — see each vendor)

- **Claude Desktop**: Free (chat only), Pro, Max (5x / 20x), Team, Enterprise — Claude Code and Cowork need Pro or above ([pricing](https://claude.com/pricing))
- **Claude Code**: Pro, Max (5x / 20x), Team, Enterprise (not Free); or Console / API billing; or via a cloud provider ([pricing](https://claude.com/pricing))
- **Cursor**: Hobby (free), Individual (Pro / Pro+ / Ultra), Teams (Standard / Premium seats), Enterprise, plus a Start plan (India only) ([pricing](https://cursor.com/pricing))
- **Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)**: Free, Pro, Max, Teams, Enterprise ([pricing](https://devin.ai/pricing))
- **GitHub Copilot**: Free, Student, Pro, Pro+, Max, Business, Enterprise (Pro free for eligible teachers / OSS maintainers) ([pricing](https://github.com/features/copilot/plans))
- **Aider**: Free (open source; you pay your model provider)
- **Continue (discontinued)**: Discontinued (code stays free under Apache 2.0)
- **Kiro (successor to Amazon Q Developer)**: Free, Pro, Pro+, Pro Max, Power, Enterprise (Amazon Q Developer: no new signups since 2026-05-15) ([pricing](https://kiro.dev/pricing))
- **Sourcegraph Cody (Enterprise only)**: Enterprise only (Cody Free / Pro ended 2025-07-23)
- **OpenAI Codex CLI**: CLI/IDE included in ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, Enterprise (Free & Go: desktop app only); or API-key billing ([pricing](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/pricing))
- **Gemini CLI**: Code Assist Standard / Enterprise licence, Vertex AI, or paid Gemini API key (free & Google AI Pro/Ultra sign-in ended 2026-06-18 → Antigravity CLI)
- **OpenCode**: Free (open source); optional [OpenCode Zen](https://opencode.ai/zen) (pay-as-you-go), [Go / Go Plus](https://opencode.ai/go) subscriptions, [Enterprise](https://opencode.ai/enterprise)
- **Cline**: Open Source (free, BYOK or Cline usage billing), Enterprise; optional ClinePass ([pricing](https://cline.bot/pricing))
- **Kilo Code**: Free & Open Source, Teams, Enterprise; optional Kilo Pass ([pricing](https://kilo.ai/pricing))
- **Qwen Code**: Free (open source); you pay your model provider
- **Amp**: Hobby (free), Individual (Megawatt / Gigawatt), Teams, Enterprise; paid credits at API prices beyond a tier ([pricing](https://ampcode.com/pricing))
- **goose**: Free (open source); you pay your model provider
- **Pi**: Free (open source); you pay your model provider or use a subscription via `/login`
- **CodeBuddy (Tencent Cloud)**: Free, Pro, Team (credits) ([pricing](https://www.codebuddy.ai/pricing))
- **Qoder (incl. Qoder CLI)**: Free, Pro, Pro+, Ultra; Teams, Enterprise (credits) ([pricing](https://qoder.com/pricing))
- **MiniMax Code**: Free (open-source CLI with BYOK); MiniMax M Plan (Go, Explore, Build) / Token Plan ([pricing](https://www.minimax.io/m-plan))
- **DeepSeek Harness (dsh)**: Free (open source); you pay your model provider (DeepSeek API is pay-as-you-go)
- **Antigravity CLI (Google Antigravity)**: Free individual quota, Google AI Pro, Google AI Ultra (AI-credit overages on Pro/Ultra); teams via Gemini Enterprise (Google Cloud) ([pricing](https://antigravity.google/pricing))

### Open source

- **Claude Desktop**: Closed (Anthropic)
- **Claude Code**: Closed — public repo has changelog, plugins and issues only (all rights reserved)
- **Cursor**: Closed (VS Code fork)
- **Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)**: Closed (Cognition; VS Code-based)
- **GitHub Copilot**: Closed (Microsoft)
- **Aider**: Apache 2.0 ✅
- **Continue (discontinued)**: Apache 2.0 — read-only, unmaintained
- **Kiro (successor to Amazon Q Developer)**: Closed (AWS)
- **Sourcegraph Cody (Enterprise only)**: Closed; last public client source archived 2025-08-01
- **OpenAI Codex CLI**: Apache 2.0 ✅
- **Gemini CLI**: Apache 2.0 ✅
- **OpenCode**: MIT ✅
- **Cline**: Apache 2.0 ✅
- **Kilo Code**: MIT ✅
- **Qwen Code**: Apache 2.0 ✅
- **Amp**: Closed (Amp Inc.)
- **goose**: Apache 2.0 ✅
- **Pi**: MIT ✅
- **CodeBuddy (Tencent Cloud)**: Closed (Tencent; proprietary CLI licence)
- **Qoder (incl. Qoder CLI)**: Closed (Alibaba)
- **MiniMax Code**: MIT ✅ (CLI; desktop app closed)
- **DeepSeek Harness (dsh)**: MIT ✅
- **Antigravity CLI (Google Antigravity)**: Closed (CLI repo is README/changelog only); Python SDK Apache 2.0 but needs a compiled runtime

### Bring your own model

- **Claude Desktop**: No — Claude models only (Enterprise can route via Google Cloud's Agent Platform or an LLM gateway)
- **Claude Code**: Claude models only — Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, or an LLM gateway
- **Cursor**: Chat only — OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Azure, Bedrock keys; Tab stays on Cursor models
- **Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)**: Model menu + Adaptive router; BYOK not documented in current Devin docs
- **GitHub Copilot**: Model picker; BYOK for any compatible provider in VS Code, Copilot CLI and the Copilot app
- **Aider**: Yes — any LLM via LiteLLM
- **Continue (discontinued)**: Yes (final release)
- **Kiro (successor to Amazon Q Developer)**: Multi-provider menu (Anthropic, OpenAI, open-weight); BYOK not documented
- **Sourcegraph Cody (Enterprise only)**: Yes (admin-configured) — BYOK via providerOverrides: OpenAI-compatible, Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, Fireworks, Google, OpenAI, HF TGI
- **OpenAI Codex CLI**: Yes — custom model providers in config.toml
- **Gemini CLI**: Gemini models (Google account, Gemini API, Vertex AI)
- **OpenCode**: Yes — 75+ providers
- **Cline**: Yes — OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and others (BYOK)
- **Kilo Code**: Yes — BYOK, or 500+ models via Kilo
- **Qwen Code**: Yes — OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and Qwen APIs; any third-party provider
- **Amp**: Amp picks the models; Model Routing sends them through your own keys, subscriptions (ChatGPT), Bedrock / Google Cloud, OpenRouter or custom URLs
- **goose**: Yes — 15+ providers, custom OpenAI/Anthropic/Ollama-compatible providers, subscriptions via ACP
- **Pi**: Yes — 15+ providers, custom providers via `models.json` or extensions
- **CodeBuddy (Tencent Cloud)**: Yes in the CLI — custom OpenAI-format models via models.json
- **Qoder (incl. Qoder CLI)**: Yes — preset providers + OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible endpoints (CLI: individual plans)
- **MiniMax Code**: Yes — any provider with base URL + API format (no MiniMax login needed)
- **DeepSeek Harness (dsh)**: Yes — DeepSeek, Anthropic, OpenAI, Kimi, GLM and custom OpenAI/Anthropic-format endpoints
- **Antigravity CLI (Google Antigravity)**: Model menu (Gemini; third-party models on Ultra); CLI accepts your own Gemini API key; no other BYOK

### Local LLM support

- **Claude Desktop**: No
- **Claude Code**: No — Anthropic doesn't support routing to non-Claude models
- **Cursor**: No official support — every request, even BYOK, goes through Cursor's backend
- **Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)**: Not documented
- **GitHub Copilot**: Yes — VS Code (Ollama extension, offline without a plan) and Copilot CLI (Ollama / vLLM / Foundry Local)
- **Aider**: Yes (Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM, LM Studio)
- **Continue (discontinued)**: Yes (final release; unmaintained)
- **Kiro (successor to Amazon Q Developer)**: Not documented
- **Sourcegraph Cody (Enterprise only)**: Self-hosted models via OpenAI-compatible / HF TGI endpoints (site admin)
- **OpenAI Codex CLI**: Yes — `--oss` with Ollama or LM Studio
- **Gemini CLI**: No — only an experimental local Gemma model for routing decisions
- **OpenCode**: Yes — Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp
- **Cline**: Yes — Ollama, LM Studio
- **Kilo Code**: Yes — Ollama, LM Studio
- **Qwen Code**: Yes — Ollama, vLLM
- **Amp**: Not documented (custom OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible URL connections exist; local use not described)
- **goose**: Yes — Ollama, LM Studio, Docker Model Runner, Ramalama
- **Pi**: Yes — llama.cpp router; Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, SGLang via `models.json`
- **CodeBuddy (Tencent Cloud)**: Yes in the CLI — OpenAI-format local endpoints (e.g. Ollama) via models.json
- **Qoder (incl. Qoder CLI)**: Not documented
- **MiniMax Code**: Yes — custom/local models via `mcode provider add`
- **DeepSeek Harness (dsh)**: Yes — via Ollama (`ollama launch dsh`) or custom local endpoints
- **Antigravity CLI (Google Antigravity)**: No in CLI / desktop / IDE (Antigravity SDK only)

### Multi-file edits / refactor

- **Claude Desktop**: Excellent — Code tab runs Claude Code (parallel sessions, visual diff review)
- **Claude Code**: Excellent — agentic, plans + executes across many files
- **Cursor**: Strong (Agent mode)
- **Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)**: Strong (Devin Local agent, replaced Cascade; same harness as Devin CLI)
- **GitHub Copilot**: Good (Agent mode in IDEs; Copilot CLI; Copilot app parallel sessions)
- **Aider**: Good — git-aware, edits in commits
- **Continue (discontinued)**: Good (final release)
- **Kiro (successor to Amazon Q Developer)**: Spec-driven: requirements → design → tasks, then the agent implements
- **Sourcegraph Cody (Enterprise only)**: Good with codebase search backing
- **OpenAI Codex CLI**: Agentic, sandboxed
- **Gemini CLI**: Agentic
- **OpenCode**: Agentic (`build` agent; read-only `plan` agent)
- **Cline**: Agentic
- **Kilo Code**: Agentic
- **Qwen Code**: Agentic (subagents, agent teams)
- **Amp**: Agentic — modes plus Search / Oracle / Librarian subagents
- **goose**: Agentic (Developer extension: shell + file editing)
- **Pi**: Agentic; minimal by design (no built-in sub-agents or plan mode — add via extensions)
- **CodeBuddy (Tencent Cloud)**: Agentic (sub-agents, agent teams)
- **Qoder (incl. Qoder CLI)**: Agentic — Quest mode, plan and goal modes, subagents
- **MiniMax Code**: Agentic (plans, permissions, session recovery)
- **DeepSeek Harness (dsh)**: Agentic (Standard mode: file editing, shell, search, planning)
- **Antigravity CLI (Google Antigravity)**: Agentic; subagents, background agents, walkthrough artifacts

### Codebase awareness

- **Claude Desktop**: Code tab: Claude Code reads the repo on demand; chat/Cowork: local folder access + MCP
- **Claude Code**: Reads files on demand, very strong with hooks
- **Cursor**: Local Instant Grep index + Explore subagent (no stored codebase embeddings)
- **Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)**: RAG-based indexing + Fast Context retrieval
- **GitHub Copilot**: Indexed for paid users
- **Aider**: Repo-map (deterministic, no embeddings)
- **Continue (discontinued)**: Indexed embeddings + custom retrievers (final release)
- **Kiro (successor to Amazon Q Developer)**: Steering files + specs
- **Sourcegraph Cody (Enterprise only)**: Sourcegraph code graph and code search across all repos
- **OpenAI Codex CLI**: AGENTS.md project instructions
- **Gemini CLI**: 1M-token context window
- **OpenCode**: LSP integration (built-in language servers feed diagnostics to the agent)
- **Cline**: @-mentions, research subagents, Memory Bank (no embeddings index)
- **Kilo Code**: Opt-in Codebase Indexing (semantic search with embeddings)
- **Qwen Code**: LSP integration, auto-memory
- **Amp**: Search subagent, AGENTS.md, Librarian for external code
- **goose**: `.goosehints` / AGENTS.md; code analysis in the Developer extension
- **Pi**: AGENTS.md / SYSTEM.md, skills; context controlled via extensions
- **CodeBuddy (Tencent Cloud)**: Cross-file understanding; memory; large-codebase / monorepo guidance
- **Qoder (incl. Qoder CLI)**: Repo Wiki, knowledge base, memory, AGENTS.md
- **MiniMax Code**: Unverified
- **DeepSeek Harness (dsh)**: LSP navigation subsystem
- **Antigravity CLI (Google Antigravity)**: AGENTS.md / GEMINI.md rules; code search

### IDE coverage

- **Claude Desktop**: Editor-agnostic — works alongside any IDE via filesystem MCP; includes Claude Code
- **Claude Code**: Terminal CLI; VS Code + JetBrains; desktop app; web (claude.ai/code); iOS/Android; Slack; GitHub Actions / GitLab CI
- **Cursor**: Standalone IDE (VS Code fork) + Agents Window; Cursor CLI; JetBrains via ACP; Cloud Agents on web / iOS
- **Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)**: Standalone IDE (VS Code-based); Devin CLI; ACP agents; JetBrains via ACP (legacy Windsurf plugins in maintenance mode)
- **GitHub Copilot**: VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains, Eclipse, Xcode, Neovim; Copilot CLI; Copilot app (desktop)
- **Aider**: Terminal CLI (works alongside any editor)
- **Continue (discontinued)**: VS Code, JetBrains, CLI (final release)
- **Kiro (successor to Amazon Q Developer)**: Kiro IDE, Kiro CLI, web, iOS, Kiro Crew; ACP editors
- **Sourcegraph Cody (Enterprise only)**: VS Code, JetBrains, Visual Studio (experimental), web, Cody CLI
- **OpenAI Codex CLI**: Terminal CLI; VS Code / Cursor / Windsurf extension; Xcode + JetBrains integrations; ChatGPT desktop app (macOS, Windows, Linux preview)
- **Gemini CLI**: Terminal CLI; VS Code companion; JetBrains + Zed via ACP
- **OpenCode**: Terminal TUI; desktop app; VS Code / Cursor / Zed / Windsurf / VSCodium extensions
- **Cline**: VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, VSCodium, Antigravity, JetBrains; CLI; desktop app (macOS, Windows beta); Kanban; SDK
- **Kilo Code**: VS Code, JetBrains, CLI, cloud
- **Qwen Code**: Terminal CLI; VS Code (beta), Zed, JetBrains; desktop app
- **Amp**: Terminal CLI; web; macOS / iOS apps; editor connection for VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Zed, Neovim
- **goose**: Desktop app; CLI; API (no IDE plugin documented)
- **Pi**: Terminal TUI; print/JSON, RPC, SDK
- **CodeBuddy (Tencent Cloud)**: CodeBuddy IDE; VS Code + JetBrains plugins; CodeBuddy Code CLI; Zed via ACP
- **Qoder (incl. Qoder CLI)**: Qoder IDE (macOS, Windows); JetBrains plugin; Qoder CLI; ACP
- **MiniMax Code**: Terminal CLI; ACP editors; desktop app
- **DeepSeek Harness (dsh)**: Local Web UI; desktop app (macOS, Windows); no IDE plugin
- **Antigravity CLI (Google Antigravity)**: Terminal CLI (`agy`); Antigravity 2.0 desktop; Antigravity IDE; VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains, Zed, Xcode extensions

### Privacy posture

- **Claude Desktop**: Account-dependent: Free / Pro / Max under Consumer Terms (training if the setting is on); Team / Enterprise / API under Commercial Terms (no training)
- **Claude Code**: Account-dependent: Free / Pro / Max under Consumer Terms (training if the setting is on); Team / Enterprise / API under Commercial Terms (no training, 30-day retention)
- **Cursor**: Privacy Mode: no training, ZDR with providers (default-on for teams); with it off Cursor may train on code data; BYOK requests still route via Cursor
- **Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)**: By default data may be used for training; paid plans can opt out (then Zero Data Retention); Enterprise never trained on without consent; SOC 2 Type II
- **GitHub Copilot**: Microsoft cloud; enterprise gates; local BYOK possible in VS Code
- **Aider**: You pick the API; can be 100% local with Ollama
- **Continue (discontinued)**: 100% local possible (final release)
- **Kiro (successor to Amazon Q Developer)**: Free and individual (incl. paid social / Builder ID) users: content may be used for service improvement unless opted out; enterprise users (IAM Identity Center / IdP): not used; individual data stored in us-east-1
- **Sourcegraph Cody (Enterprise only)**: Enterprise: Sourcegraph will not train on your company's data; LLM providers do not train on your codebase
- **OpenAI Codex CLI**: OpenAI cloud (ChatGPT or API terms), or fully local with `--oss`
- **Gemini CLI**: Google cloud; terms depend on sign-in method (Code Assist Standard/Enterprise, Gemini API, Vertex AI)
- **OpenCode**: You pick the provider; can be fully local
- **Cline**: BYOK — code goes to the provider you choose; can be fully local
- **Kilo Code**: BYOK or Kilo-routed models; can be fully local
- **Qwen Code**: You pick the provider; can be fully local
- **Amp**: No training unless you opt in (never on Enterprise); minimal data retention with providers; SOC 2 Type II
- **goose**: Runs locally; code goes to the provider you choose; can be fully local
- **Pi**: You pick the provider; can be fully local
- **CodeBuddy (Tencent Cloud)**: Unverified — docs state only general measures; CLI README: feedback not used for model training
- **Qoder (incl. Qoder CLI)**: Singapore operator; data stored in US, Singapore, Japan; LLM providers incl. Qwen and Kimi; training policy unverified
- **MiniMax Code**: MiniMax account or the provider you choose; can be fully local with BYOK
- **DeepSeek Harness (dsh)**: Runs locally; code goes to the provider you choose; can be fully local
- **Antigravity CLI (Google Antigravity)**: Individual: interactions used to improve Google products (human review possible; opt-out in Settings); Enterprise: Google Cloud terms

### Best use case

- **Claude Desktop**: Architecture / planning sessions, visual debugging, MCP-extended workflows alongside any editor
- **Claude Code**: Power users, big refactors, terminal-first workflows, CI integration
- **Cursor**: Polished IDE replacement, broad audience
- **Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)**: Cursor alternative, especially alongside Devin cloud agents
- **GitHub Copilot**: Already on GitHub, want zero friction
- **Aider**: Open-source / local-first / git discipline (note: development has slowed)
- **Continue (discontinued)**: Migrating off it, or forking the Apache-2.0 code
- **Kiro (successor to Amazon Q Developer)**: AWS shops, spec-first teams, Amazon Q Developer migrations
- **Sourcegraph Cody (Enterprise only)**: Enterprises on Sourcegraph with massive monorepos
- **OpenAI Codex CLI**: ChatGPT subscribers; open-source terminal agent with a sandbox
- **Gemini CLI**: Google Cloud / Code Assist teams; open-source Gemini terminal agent with very large context
- **OpenCode**: Vendor-neutral open-source terminal agent; fully local setups
- **Cline**: Open-source agent inside your existing editor
- **Kilo Code**: One open-source agent across VS Code, JetBrains and terminal
- **Qwen Code**: Qwen-model users; open-source agent with local models
- **Amp**: Multi-model agent with remote orbs and shared team threads
- **goose**: Open-source local agent with a desktop UI and MCP extensions
- **Pi**: Minimal, hackable harness you extend yourself
- **CodeBuddy (Tencent Cloud)**: Tencent Cloud / WeChat-ecosystem teams; CLI agent with custom model endpoints
- **Qoder (incl. Qoder CLI)**: Delegated long-running tasks; Qwen-ecosystem teams
- **MiniMax Code**: MiniMax model users; MIT terminal agent with BYOK
- **DeepSeek Harness (dsh)**: DeepSeek users; plugin-built custom harnesses
- **Antigravity CLI (Google Antigravity)**: Free Google terminal agent; former Gemini CLI free / Pro / Ultra users


## Tools


## Aider

URL: https://aider.chat
Repo: https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider
License: open-source  Deployment: cli

_AI pair programming in your terminal — edits code across your git repo with commit-per-change discipline._

Aider is an open-source CLI coding assistant that edits code in an
existing git repository under the developer's direction. It's known for
two core design choices: it operates on git (every change becomes a
discrete commit with an auto-generated message, making rollback trivial),
and it builds a "repo map" of the codebase so the model always has
context for where functions and types live across files.

It supports any LLM provider — Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT, local models
via Ollama or OpenAI-compatible servers, DeepSeek, xAI. Unlike IDE-coupled
assistants, Aider lives in the terminal and plays well with any editor
the developer already uses.

The `/architect` mode separates planning (using a reasoning model) from
editing (using a fast edit model) for complex changes. The benchmark
leaderboard Aider maintains is a widely-cited reference for LLM coding
performance. Images (screenshots, mockups) and web pages can be added to
the chat for vision-capable models.

Staleness note (checked 2026-10-05): the latest tagged release is v0.86.0
from 2025-08-09, and the last commit to the main branch is from
2026-05-22. Aider still works and its docs are online, but development has
slowed sharply — weigh that before standardising on it.

Features:
- Git-first workflow with automatic commits per change
- Repo-map context for large codebase awareness
- Any LLM provider (Claude, GPT, local, DeepSeek, xAI)
- Architect mode: reasoning model plans, edit model executes
- Image and web-page input for vision-capable models
- Voice input support
- In-chat commands for file management, linting, testing
- Language-agnostic (Python, JS, Rust, Go, Java, C++, … )

Best for:
- Pair programming in the terminal without IDE lock-in
- Refactoring across multi-file changes with git discipline
- Adding features to existing codebases with reviewable commits
- Running local LLMs as coding assistants
- Developers who prefer vim / emacs over IDE-integrated assistants

---

## Amp

URL: https://ampcode.com
License: commercial  Deployment: cli

_Multi-model coding agent from Amp Inc. (spun out of Sourcegraph) — terminal CLI, web and Mac/iOS apps, with remote "orbs" that keep working after you close the laptop._

Amp describes itself as "a coding agent and development environment built
for the frontier". It began inside Sourcegraph and became a separate
company on 2025-12-02 ("Amp is becoming a separate company. We're spinning
out of Sourcegraph"). It is closed source.

Amp chooses the models: its main agent runs frontier models (GPT-5.6,
Claude Fable 5.1 and fast models at the time of writing), with four modes
on "the Dial" (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `ultra`) and specialist subagents
(Search, Oracle, Librarian). Model Routing lets you send some or all models
through your own API keys, ChatGPT or other subscriptions, cloud platforms
(Bedrock, Google Cloud) or gateways (OpenRouter, Ollama Cloud, any
OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible URL).

The same threads run in the terminal CLI (`amp`; macOS, Linux, Windows via
WSL), on the web, and in the macOS / iOS apps. Work can run locally, on your
own "runners", or in "orbs" — remote machines Amp creates per thread. The
CLI connects to VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Zed and Neovim. It supports MCP,
plugins, skills and AGENTS.md, and images can be pasted or dragged into the
prompt.

Tiers are Hobby (free), Individual (Megawatt / Gigawatt), Teams and
Enterprise; usage beyond a tier is paid credits at provider API prices. The
former ad-supported "Amp Free" daily grant has been paused or reduced for
many users since 2026-05-23. Amp states that neither it nor its
subprocessors train on your data unless you opt in, and it is SOC 2 Type II.

Features:
- Terminal CLI `amp` (macOS, Linux, Windows via WSL); web; macOS and iOS apps
- Orbs (per-thread remote machines) and self-hosted runners
- Modes low / medium / high / ultra; Search, Oracle and Librarian subagents
- Model Routing — own keys, ChatGPT and other subscriptions, Bedrock / Google Cloud, OpenRouter and custom endpoints
- Editor connection for VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Zed, Neovim
- MCP, plugins, skills, AGENTS.md; TypeScript and Python SDKs
- Shared threads, multiplayer and workspaces for teams
- Plans — Hobby (free), Individual (Megawatt / Gigawatt), Teams, Enterprise

Best for:
- Developers who want the agent to pick frontier models per task
- Long-running tasks that continue on a remote machine
- Teams that share and review agent threads

---

## Antigravity CLI (Google Antigravity)

URL: https://antigravity.google
License: commercial  Deployment: cli

_Google's `agy` terminal agent — part of Google Antigravity (desktop app, IDE, editor extensions on one harness) and the successor to Gemini CLI for free and Google AI Pro/Ultra users._

Antigravity CLI (`agy`) is "the lightweight Terminal User Interface (TUI)
surface of Antigravity", built in Go. It shares one agent harness and one
set of settings with the rest of Google Antigravity: the Antigravity 2.0
desktop app, the Antigravity IDE, extensions for VS Code, Visual Studio,
JetBrains IDEs, Zed and Xcode, and a Python SDK. Conversations started in
the CLI can continue in Antigravity 2.0.

On 2026-06-18 Antigravity CLI replaced Gemini CLI for free and Google AI
Pro/Ultra users. It imports Gemini CLI extensions (as plugins), skills,
settings and MCP servers, and still reads `GEMINI.md` and `AGENTS.md`.

It runs natively on macOS, Linux and Windows. All individual accounts get
Gemini models with a weekly-limited quota; Google AI Pro and Ultra raise
the limits and allow AI-credit overages, and Ultra adds third-party models.
Teams use it under Google Cloud terms via Gemini Enterprise. There is no
bring-your-own-key for other providers, but the CLI can run on your own
Gemini API key. Individual-tier interactions may be used to improve Google
products (opt out in Settings). Closed source: the GitHub repo holds only
the README, changelog and examples.

Features:
- Terminal CLI `agy` (Go), native on macOS, Linux and Windows; headless `agy -p`
- Same harness as the Antigravity 2.0 desktop app and Antigravity IDE
- Extensions for VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains, Zed, Xcode
- Plans — free individual quota, Google AI Pro, Google AI Ultra; Gemini Enterprise for teams
- Gemini models (third-party models on Ultra); own Gemini API key supported in the CLI
- MCP, plugins, skills, hooks, subagents; imports Gemini CLI setups
- Image paste into the prompt

Best for:
- Former Gemini CLI free and Google AI Pro/Ultra users
- A no-cost Google terminal agent with a weekly quota
- Moving between terminal, desktop app and editor on one Google harness

---

## Claude Code

URL: https://claude.com/product/claude-code
License: commercial  Deployment: cli

_Anthropic's terminal-first agentic coding assistant with deep tool use and codebase awareness._

Claude Code is Anthropic's official agentic coding tool, available in the
terminal, IDEs (VS Code, JetBrains), the Claude desktop app, the browser
(cloud sessions at claude.ai/code) and the Claude iOS/Android app. It runs
only Claude models — via Anthropic directly or via Amazon Bedrock, Claude
Platform on AWS, Google Cloud's Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI) or
Microsoft Foundry, optionally through an LLM gateway — and has first-class
tool use for reading
and editing files, running shell commands, searching codebases, browsing
the web, and orchestrating sub-agents. It ships with a hook system, slash
commands, MCP server support, and IDE integrations (VS Code, JetBrains).

Unlike chat-only coding assistants, Claude Code is agentic by design: it
plans, executes multi-step changes, reads its own output, and recovers
from errors. The Claude Agent SDK (Python and TypeScript) gives developers
the same tools, agent loop and context management that power Claude Code.
The public GitHub repo hosts the changelog, official plugins and the issue
tracker, not the source.

Privacy depends on how you sign in. With a Free, Pro or Max account,
Claude Code falls under Anthropic's Consumer Terms: data is used to train
future models when the account's model-improvement setting is on (5-year
retention; 30 days if off). Under the Commercial Terms (Team, Enterprise,
API and cloud platforms), Anthropic does not train on Claude Code prompts
or code and retains them for 30 days by default. Claude Code is included
in Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise (not Free), or billed through a Claude
Console/API account or a cloud provider.

Images can be dragged in, pasted (Ctrl+V; Alt+V on Windows/WSL) or
referenced by file path in a session.

Anthropic publishes both `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` for the Claude
Code documentation at code.claude.com, making it one of the best-indexed
coding-agent references available to other AI assistants.

Features:
- Terminal CLI with native tool use (Bash, Read, Edit, Write, Grep)
- Hook system for shaping agent behavior per-project
- Slash commands and user-defined skills via SKILL.md
- MCP server support for connecting external tools and data
- IDE integrations for VS Code and JetBrains; also in the desktop app, on the web (cloud sessions) and on iOS/Android
- Image input (drag-and-drop, paste or file path)
- Background task support and session persistence
- Claude Agent SDK exposes Claude Code's agent loop and tools for custom agents

Best for:
- Refactoring and migration across large codebases
- Debugging and fixing issues with full shell + git access
- Writing new features with reviewed commits and CI awareness
- Onboarding to unfamiliar repos via guided exploration
- Building and testing in one loop without leaving the terminal

---

## Claude Desktop

URL: https://claude.com/download
License: commercial  Deployment: local

_Anthropic's desktop app (macOS, Windows, Linux beta) combining chat, Cowork agentic tasks and Claude Code, extensible via MCP, skills and plugins._

Claude Desktop is Anthropic's official native app for macOS, Windows,
and Linux (beta; Ubuntu 22.04+ / Debian 12+). While not exclusively a
coding tool, it combines: MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers that give
it filesystem, git, GitHub, database, and shell access; a skills system
for packaging repeatable coding workflows; the Code tab (Claude Code
inside Desktop) and Cowork for autonomous multi-step tasks; long-context
conversations synced to your Claude account; and Anthropic's current
Claude models (Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 4.5) running
underneath.

Compared to **Claude Code** (Anthropic's terminal CLI agent): same
underlying models and tool-use primitives, different interface. Claude
Desktop is faster for visual work (drop in screenshots, read PDFs,
inspect designs), and the chat-first UX suits multi-turn coding
sessions where you're thinking through architecture rather than
typing-to-edit. Claude Code wins for terminal-native workflows and
CI integration; Claude Desktop wins for the "I want to talk through
a problem with full repo access" mode.

Compared to **Cursor / Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)**: those are
IDE-bound. Claude Desktop is editor-agnostic — works alongside any editor
(VS Code, JetBrains, Neovim) by reading/writing files via MCP. In the
Code tab, Claude Code edits files directly, with a visual diff viewer,
integrated terminal and file editor.

Plus: Claude Desktop is the place where MCP server experimentation
happens. New community MCP servers ship constantly (puppeteer, Stripe,
Slack, Postgres, Sentry, ...) — adding any of them gives Claude
Desktop a new capability without changing the app.

Features:
- Native apps for macOS, Windows and Linux (beta; Ubuntu 22.04+ / Debian 12+)
- MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration — filesystem, git, GitHub, postgres, shell, browser, custom servers
- Skills system — package coding workflows as reusable invocations
- Code tab (Claude Code) and Cowork for autonomous multi-step tasks (Pro and above)
- Drop in screenshots / PDFs for visual debugging
- Long-context conversations synced to your Claude account
- Multiple models (Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) selectable; Fable on paid plans
- Editor-agnostic — pairs with any IDE you already use

Best for:
- Architecture / planning sessions where you talk through a design
- Multi-file refactors driven by chat with the agent reading the repo
- Visual debugging — drop in a screenshot of a broken UI
- Workflow automation via custom MCP servers and skills
- Power users who want Claude's full capabilities without committing to a CLI or new IDE
- Working alongside an existing editor (VS Code / JetBrains / Neovim) without replacing it

---

## Cline

URL: https://cline.bot
Repo: https://github.com/cline/cline
License: open-source  Deployment: local

_Apache-2.0 coding agent for VS Code-family editors and JetBrains, with a CLI and desktop app — bring your own keys or run local models._

Cline is "the open source coding agent in your IDE, terminal, & desktop",
licensed Apache 2.0. The extension installs into VS Code, Cursor,
Windsurf, VSCodium, Antigravity and JetBrains IDEs (JetBrains is listed
as an Enterprise feature on the pricing page); there is also a CLI
(interactive or headless for CI/CD), a desktop app (macOS; Windows beta)
for open-weight models, Kanban (preview) and an SDK (`@cline/sdk`).

The open-source version is free and runs on your own API keys ("OpenAI,
Anthropic, Google, and others"), on Cline's usage-billing provider, or on
local models via Ollama and LM Studio. ClinePass is an optional
subscription for open models. An Enterprise tier adds team management,
SSO, audit logs and VPC deployment.

It supports MCP servers and plugins, and can scaffold new MCP tools on
request.

Features:
- Extension for VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, VSCodium, Antigravity, JetBrains (listed as an Enterprise feature on the pricing page)
- CLI (interactive or headless) and desktop app (macOS; Windows beta)
- Kanban (preview) and SDK (`@cline/sdk`)
- Bring your own API keys; local models via Ollama / LM Studio
- MCP servers and plugins
- Plans — Open Source (free) and Enterprise; optional ClinePass subscription for open models

Best for:
- Open-source agent inside an existing editor
- Teams that need BYOK with enterprise controls
- Local-model setups for code that can't leave the machine

## CodeBuddy (Tencent Cloud)

URL: https://www.codebuddy.ai
License: commercial  Deployment: local

_Tencent Cloud's AI coding assistant — CodeBuddy IDE, VS Code and JetBrains plugins, and the CodeBuddy Code terminal agent with MCP and custom (incl. local) models._

CodeBuddy is Tencent Cloud's coding assistant ("Tencent Cloud Code
Assistant"), with a China site at codebuddy.cn / copilot.tencent.com and an
international site at codebuddy.ai. It comes in three forms: CodeBuddy IDE
(Windows and macOS), plugins for VS Code and JetBrains IDEs, and CodeBuddy
Code, a terminal agent (`codebuddy` / `cbc`).

CodeBuddy Code installs via npm (`@tencent-ai/codebuddy-code`), Homebrew or
a native binary (beta) for macOS, Linux (x86_64 / arm64) and Windows. It
supports MCP, sub-agents, agent teams, skills, hooks, plugins, headless
mode, an HTTP API, an SDK (Python / TypeScript) and ACP for Zed. Custom
models can be added in `models.json` with any OpenAI-format endpoint,
including a local server such as Ollama, and images can be sent to
vision models.

Individual plans are Free and Pro, plus a Team plan; usage is metered in
credits. The CLI is distributed under a proprietary licence.

Features:
- CodeBuddy IDE (Windows, macOS); VS Code and JetBrains plugins
- CodeBuddy Code CLI (npm, Homebrew, native binary for macOS / Linux / Windows)
- MCP, sub-agents, agent teams, skills, hooks, plugins, SDK, ACP (Zed)
- Custom OpenAI-format models via models.json, including local endpoints
- Image input for vision models
- Plans — Free, Pro, Team

Best for:
- Teams in the Tencent Cloud / WeCom ecosystem
- A Claude Code-style terminal agent with custom or local model endpoints
- IDE plugin plus terminal agent from one vendor

## Continue (discontinued)

URL: https://www.continue.dev
Repo: https://github.com/continuedev/continue
License: open-source  Deployment: local

_DISCONTINUED — Continue was acquired by Cursor in mid-2026; the Apache-2.0 repo is now read-only and no longer maintained._

Continue was an open-source (Apache 2.0) coding agent for VS Code,
JetBrains and the terminal, best known for bring-your-own-model
configuration and first-class local LLM support (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM).

It has been discontinued. continue.dev now reads "Continue was acquired by
Cursor", and the repository README states that it "is no longer actively
maintained and is read-only for all users". The team shipped final
releases (final published builds: VS Code extension 2.0.0 stable / 2.1.0
pre-release, tagged 2026-06-19; CLI 1.5.47 on npm, 2026-06-18; JetBrains
plugin 1.0.67). The source stays available under
Apache 2.0, so existing installs keep working and the code can be forked,
but there will be no fixes, new model support or security updates.

Kept on this list as a pointer for people searching for it. For an
actively maintained open-source, bring-your-own-model alternative, see
Cline, Kilo Code, OpenCode or Qwen Code.

Continue's `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` have returned 404 since at least
2026-07-24.

Features:
- Final releases: VS Code extension 2.0.0 (2026-06-19), CLI 1.5.47, JetBrains plugin 1.0.67
- Source remains Apache 2.0 on GitHub (read-only)
- No further maintenance

Best for:
- Existing users planning a migration
- Forks that want an Apache-2.0 IDE-agent codebase to build on

---

## Cursor

URL: https://cursor.com
License: commercial  Deployment: local

_AI-first fork of VS Code with deep LLM integration, agent mode, and codebase-aware context._

Cursor is a commercial fork of VS Code that puts AI coding assistance at
the center of the editor rather than as an extension. It ships chat,
inline edits, multi-file rewrites, autocomplete, an agent mode for
autonomous task execution, and codebase-wide context retrieval out of the
box — running Cursor's own models (Composer 2.5, Grok 4.7) alongside
OpenAI, Anthropic and Google models.

Cursor differentiates on UX polish: @-mentions to reference files and
symbols, diff-style inline edits, a native command palette for AI
actions, and proprietary context-selection heuristics. Codebase search
uses a local Instant Grep index and an Explore subagent; Cursor "does not
store embeddings of your codebase for search". Its Agent (formerly
"Composer"; Composer is now Cursor's in-house model) can execute
multi-step refactors across many files with user approval gates.

It's closed-source and subscription-based. Plans are Hobby (free),
Individual (Pro / Pro+ / Ultra), Teams (Standard / Premium seats),
Enterprise, plus a Start plan (India only); paid plans include MCPs,
skills, hooks and cloud agents. A terminal agent, Cursor CLI (`agent`),
ships alongside the editor, together with an Agents Window, Cloud Agents
(web / iOS) and JetBrains support via ACP. Bring-your-own API keys
(OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Azure, AWS Bedrock) work for chat models
only — per Cursor's docs, Tab completion stays on Cursor's built-in
models.

Ownership changed in 2026: "Cursor has officially been acquired by SpaceX"
(Cursor blog, 2026-08-14), completing a process that began with a SpaceXAI
model-training partnership in April. The product keeps its name. Cursor
also acquired Continue in mid-2026 (see that entry).

Features:
- VS Code fork with preserved extension compatibility
- Chat with @-file, @-symbol, @-web context references
- Inline edit with diff-preview before applying
- Agent mode for multi-step autonomous refactors
- Codebase search via a local Instant Grep index and an Explore subagent
- Tab autocomplete (runs on Cursor's built-in models)
- Cursor models (Composer, Grok) plus OpenAI, Anthropic and Google models
- Cursor CLI (`agent`) for terminal use
- Agents Window, Cloud Agents (web / iOS) and JetBrains via ACP
- MCP support

Best for:
- Professional developers who want maximum AI integration
- Teams that want a consistent IDE across members with built-in AI
- Large refactors that benefit from multi-file agent coordination
- Developers migrating from pure VS Code who want more AI than extensions provide

## DeepSeek Harness (dsh)

URL: https://deepseek.com/harness
Repo: https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness
License: open-source  Deployment: local

_DeepSeek's MIT-licensed "everything is a plugin" agent harness — a coding agent out of the box, run as a local Web UI or desktop app, with DeepSeek, other providers or local models._

DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) is "an open-source agent harness developed by
DeepSeek AI", MIT-licensed and built on an everything-is-a-plugin
architecture powered by the Cordis plugin runtime: models, tools, skills,
sessions, sandboxes, the agent loop and the UI are all plugins you can
swap. It is in developer preview, and the README warns of
compatibility-breaking changes.

It runs as a local Web UI (`npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web`, needs Node.js) or as
a desktop app (macOS 13+ on Apple silicon, Windows 10+ x64). Models: a
DeepSeek API key, bundled third-party providers (e.g. Anthropic, OpenAI,
Moonshot/Kimi, Z.ai/GLM), or any custom OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI
Responses or Anthropic Messages endpoint; images can be enabled per model.
Ollama documents `ollama launch dsh` for local and Ollama Cloud models.

It connects MCP servers (stdio or Streamable HTTP), and its tool subsystems
include bash, PTY sessions, background jobs, LSP navigation, web access,
skills and workflows.

Features:
- Everything-is-a-plugin harness on Cordis; create plugins by conversation
- Local Web UI via npx; desktop app (macOS Apple silicon, Windows)
- DeepSeek, bundled third-party providers, custom OpenAI/Anthropic-format endpoints
- Local models via Ollama (`ollama launch dsh`)
- MCP (stdio, Streamable HTTP), LSP navigation, subagents, scheduled tasks
- MIT licence; developer preview

Best for:
- DeepSeek model users who want a first-party agent
- Building a custom agent harness from swappable plugins
- Local-model agent work through Ollama

## Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)

URL: https://devin.ai/desktop
License: commercial  Deployment: local

_Cognition's AI-native IDE — the product formerly called Windsurf (and before that, Codeium), now built around the Devin Local agent._

Devin Desktop is the product that used to be called Windsurf. Cognition
(the company behind the Devin cloud agent) acquired Windsurf's "IP,
product, trademark and brand" on 2025-07-14, after Google hired Windsurf's
CEO and licensed its technology. On 2026-06-02 Windsurf was renamed Devin
Desktop via an over-the-air update: same editor, settings and extensions,
and — per Cognition — the same plans. windsurf.com and codeium.com now
redirect to devin.ai/desktop.

The rename also replaced the agent. Cascade, Windsurf's original agent,
was succeeded by Devin Local, rewritten from scratch in Rust; the legacy
Cascade agent remained available through July 2026. Devin Local shares
its agent harness with Devin CLI, Cognition's terminal agent (macOS,
Linux, WSL, Windows), which can hand tasks off to Devin Cloud. The editor
now positions itself as a command center for local and cloud agents
(including Devin itself) and speaks the Agent Client Protocol (ACP).

The old Codeium autocomplete extensions live on as "Windsurf plugins", but
Cognition's docs put the VS Code, Vim/Neovim, Visual Studio, Jupyter,
Chrome and Eclipse plugins in maintenance mode, and say of the JetBrains
plugin that "Cascade is being deprecated"; for JetBrains the FAQ now
recommends Devin over ACP. This list no longer carries a separate Codeium
entry.

Features:
- VS Code-based IDE (backwards-compatible with Windsurf and VS Code extensions)
- Devin Local agent (replaced Cascade in June–July 2026)
- Devin CLI — the same agent harness in the terminal (macOS, Linux, WSL, Windows)
- Agent Command Center for managing local and cloud agents
- MCP server integration
- RAG-based codebase indexing and Fast Context retrieval
- Model menu (SWE-2, Claude, GPT, Gemini, Grok) with the Adaptive router
- Plans — Free, Pro, Max, Teams, Enterprise

Best for:
- Developers who want a Cursor-style AI IDE from a different vendor
- Teams that also use Devin cloud agents and want one place to manage both
- Former Windsurf / Codeium users (the update carried settings forward)

## Gemini CLI

URL: https://geminicli.com
Repo: https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli
License: open-source  Deployment: cli

_Google's open-source (Apache 2.0) terminal agent for Gemini models — now for Code Assist Standard/Enterprise, Google Cloud and paid Gemini API key users; free and Google AI Pro/Ultra users moved to Antigravity CLI on 2026-06-18._

Gemini CLI is "an open-source AI agent that brings the power of Gemini
directly into your terminal", licensed Apache 2.0. It runs Gemini 3
models with a 1M-token context window and can build from PDFs, images or
sketches using Gemini's multimodal input.

Since 2026-06-18 Gemini CLI no longer serves free (Gemini Code Assist for
individuals) or Google AI Pro/Ultra sign-ins — Google moved those users to
Antigravity CLI. It remains supported for organisations with a Gemini
Code Assist Standard or Enterprise licence, through Google Cloud / Vertex
AI, and with paid Gemini API keys. Which privacy terms apply depends on
that sign-in method (Code Assist, Gemini API or Google Cloud).

It supports MCP servers and extensions. Editor integration is via the
Gemini CLI Companion extension for VS Code-compatible IDEs, and via the
Agent Client Protocol for JetBrains IDEs, Zed and other ACP editors.

Features:
- Terminal agent, Apache 2.0
- Code Assist Standard/Enterprise licence, Vertex AI or paid Gemini API key (free and Google AI Pro/Ultra sign-in ended 2026-06-18)
- Gemini 3 models, 1M-token context
- Multimodal input (images, PDFs, sketches)
- MCP servers and extensions
- VS Code companion extension; ACP for JetBrains and Zed

Best for:
- Teams on Gemini Code Assist Standard/Enterprise or Google Cloud who want an open-source, auditable terminal agent
- Google Cloud / Vertex AI shops
- Very large context tasks (whole-repo reading)

## GitHub Copilot

URL: https://github.com/features/copilot
License: commercial  Deployment: local

_GitHub's native AI coding assistant with chat, autocomplete, and agent mode across major IDEs._

GitHub Copilot is the original and most widely deployed AI coding
assistant, integrated natively into VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains
IDEs, Eclipse, Xcode, Neovim, and GitHub itself. It offers inline code
completion, chat, a multi-file agent mode, pull-request summaries, and a
terminal agent, GitHub Copilot CLI (`copilot`), which ships with the
GitHub MCP server preconfigured and accepts additional MCP servers. The
older `gh copilot` extension was deprecated on 2025-10-25 in favour of
Copilot CLI. Copilot CLI runs on Linux, macOS and Windows (PowerShell and
WSL), accepts image and PDF attachments, and supports BYOK including
local models (OpenAI-compatible endpoints, Ollama, vLLM, Foundry Local,
Azure OpenAI, Anthropic). The GitHub Copilot app, a desktop app built on
Copilot CLI for macOS, Linux and Windows, runs parallel agent sessions
and is available in all plans.

Under the hood Copilot routes to multiple LLMs — GPT, Claude Sonnet,
Gemini — with model choice exposed to users on the paid tiers. In VS Code,
Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) connects any compatible model provider, including
local models via the Ollama extension; per the VS Code docs, "You can use a
local model completely offline", and BYOK models work without a Copilot
plan or GitHub sign-in (Business/Enterprise admins can disable BYOK). Its
reach within the GitHub platform (issues, PRs, code review, Actions)
makes it a practical default for teams already on GitHub.

For enterprise deployments, Copilot offers SOC 2 compliance, data
residency, code reference filtering, and the ability to restrict
external traffic.

Features:
- VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains, Eclipse, Xcode, Neovim integrations
- Inline autocomplete, chat, and multi-file agent mode
- Pull-request and code-review assistance on GitHub
- Multiple model backends (GPT, Claude, Gemini)
- GitHub Copilot CLI (`copilot`) — terminal agent with MCP, BYOK and local models via Ollama (replaced `gh copilot`)
- GitHub Copilot app — desktop app for parallel agent sessions, built on Copilot CLI (macOS, Linux, Windows)
- BYOK and offline local models in VS Code (Ollama extension)
- Enterprise tier with SOC 2, data residency, content filtering
- Plans — Free, Student, Pro, Pro+, Max, Business, Enterprise (free Copilot Pro for eligible teachers and popular-OSS maintainers)

Best for:
- Professional development at organizations already on GitHub
- Teams needing enterprise compliance posture out of the box
- Users who want PR / issue / code-review AI integrated into Git workflow
- Cross-IDE consistency (one subscription, many editors)
- Students and OSS maintainers on the free tier

## goose

URL: https://goose-docs.ai
Repo: https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose
License: open-source  Deployment: local

_Apache-2.0 local AI agent (desktop app, CLI and API) started by Block and now part of the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation — 15+ providers, local models and MCP extensions._

goose is "your native open source AI agent — desktop app, CLI, and API —
for code, workflows, and everything in between", written in Rust and
licensed Apache 2.0. Block created it; it is now "part of the Agentic AI
Foundation (AAIF) at the Linux Foundation", and the repository moved from
`block/goose` to `aaif-goose/goose` (the old URL redirects). The docs moved
from block.github.io/goose to goose-docs.ai.

It runs on your machine, with a native desktop app and a CLI for macOS,
Linux and Windows (native Windows install via Git Bash or PowerShell; WSL
optional). It works with "15+ providers — Anthropic, OpenAI, Google,
Ollama, OpenRouter, Azure, Bedrock, and more", can use existing Claude,
ChatGPT or Gemini subscriptions via ACP, and runs local models through
Ollama, LM Studio, Docker Model Runner, Ramalama and other
OpenAI-compatible servers.

Capabilities come from MCP extensions (70+), reusable recipes, subagents
and project hints (`.goosehints` / AGENTS.md).

Features:
- Desktop app and CLI for macOS, Linux and Windows; embeddable API
- 15+ providers; subscriptions via ACP; local models via Ollama, LM Studio, Docker Model Runner, Ramalama
- MCP extensions (70+), built-in Developer extension for shell and file editing
- Recipes (shareable task templates), sessions, `.goosehints` / AGENTS.md
- Apache 2.0, governed under the Agentic AI Foundation (Linux Foundation)

Best for:
- Open-source, vendor-neutral agent with a desktop UI as well as a CLI
- Fully local agent work with open-weight models
- Automations shared as recipes across a team

## Kilo Code

URL: https://kilo.ai
Repo: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode
License: open-source  Deployment: local

_MIT-licensed coding agent for VS Code, JetBrains and the CLI with 500+ models, BYOK and local models._

Kilo Code is an MIT-licensed coding agent that "meets you everywhere you
work": VS Code, JetBrains, the CLI, and a cloud surface at app.kilo.ai.
The Kilo CLI is a fork of OpenCode.

Kilo's pricing page lists a free and open-source tier (VS Code, JetBrains
and CLI extensions), plus Teams and Enterprise (14-day Enterprise
trial). You can "Bring your own Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Azure, AWS
Bedrock, or other provider keys" and "Run local models with Ollama or
LM Studio"; through a Kilo account (Kilo Gateway, or the optional Kilo
Pass) there are 500+ models with mid-task switching. Opt-in Codebase
Indexing adds semantic search with embeddings.

A Kilo Marketplace distributes agents, skills, MCP servers and plugins.

Kilo's `llms.txt` is served, but as of 2026-10-05 its page links point
at `kilocode-docs.vercel.app` raw-markdown URLs that return 404, so it is
of limited use to agents.

Features:
- VS Code and JetBrains extensions, CLI (OpenCode fork), cloud agents
- 500+ models; BYOK for major providers
- Local models via Ollama or LM Studio
- Opt-in Codebase Indexing (semantic search)
- Marketplace for agents, skills, MCP servers, plugins
- Plans — Free & Open Source, Teams, Enterprise; optional Kilo Pass for inference

Best for:
- One open-source agent across VS Code, JetBrains and terminal
- Teams that want BYOK and model choice with central billing
- Local-model workflows

## Kiro (successor to Amazon Q Developer)

URL: https://kiro.dev
License: commercial  Deployment: local

_AWS's spec-driven coding agent (IDE, CLI, web) — the replacement for Amazon Q Developer, whose IDE plugins reach end of support on 2027-04-30._

Kiro is AWS's AI coding agent, built around one agent harness shared by
the Kiro IDE, the Kiro CLI, a web surface, iOS (TestFlight early access),
Kiro Crew (a multi-agent personal agent for macOS, Linux and Windows)
and any ACP-compatible editor. Its distinguishing idea is
spec-driven development: a feature is
planned as requirements, design and tasks before the agent implements it,
with steering files and event-driven hooks shaping the agent's behaviour.

Kiro is what AWS points Amazon Q Developer users to. Per AWS's end-of-support
announcement, new Q Developer Free Tier accounts and subscriptions were
blocked from 2026-05-15, and "Amazon Q Developer IDE plugins and paid
Subscriptions will reach end of support on April 30, 2027, giving customers
12 months to transition to Kiro." The Q Developer CLI has already become
Kiro CLI — Kiro's docs call it "the next update of the Q CLI", with
existing workflows, subscription and authentication carried over. Kiro
CLI runs on macOS, Linux and Windows 11 (PowerShell).

Models come from several providers (Anthropic, OpenAI and open-weight
families such as DeepSeek, GLM, MiniMax and Qwen). The docs we checked do
not describe bring-your-own-key or local-model support. The public GitHub
repository (kirodotdev/Kiro) is an issue and feedback tracker; the
product source is not hosted there.

Features:
- Spec-driven development (requirements → design → tasks)
- Steering files and event-driven agent hooks
- MCP support
- Kiro IDE, Kiro CLI (successor to Amazon Q Developer CLI), web, iOS and Kiro Crew
- ACP support for other editors
- Multi-provider model menu (Anthropic, OpenAI, open-weight models)
- Plans — Free, Pro, Pro+, Pro Max, Power, Enterprise

Best for:
- Amazon Q Developer users migrating before the 2027-04-30 end of support
- Teams that want a written spec before the agent touches code
- AWS-centric organisations standardising on an AWS-supported agent

---

## MiniMax Code

URL: https://agent.minimax.io/docs/cli/quick-start
Repo: https://github.com/MiniMax-AI/minimax-code
License: open-source  Deployment: cli

_MiniMax's coding agent — an MIT-licensed terminal CLI (`mcode`) plus a desktop app, running MiniMax models on an M Plan or any compatible model you bring._

MiniMax Code is MiniMax's agent product: a desktop app (macOS, Windows)
for software development and other tasks, and MiniMax Code CLI, a terminal
agent run as `mcode`. The CLI source — terminal TUI, headless CLI and ACP
components — is open on GitHub under MIT for first-party code; the desktop
app is distributed separately. The repo's licence notes say some terminal
code derives from Pi and keeps its original licence declarations.

The CLI installs with a one-line script on macOS, Linux and WSL, a
PowerShell script on Windows, or npm (`@minimax-ai/code`). You either sign
in with a MiniMax account (mainland China or Global region) or bring your
own key — "BYOK does not require a MiniMax login" — by adding any provider
with a base URL, API format and model name, including custom/local models.
It offers interactive, headless (`mcode exec`) and ACP modes, with skills,
MCP and plugins.

MiniMax's subscription is M Plan (tiers Go, Explore, Build; built on the
earlier Token Plan), which also works in other tools such as Claude Code,
Codex, Cursor and OpenCode.

Features:
- Terminal CLI `mcode` (macOS, Linux, WSL, Windows); MIT first-party source
- Desktop app for macOS and Windows (closed, separate)
- MiniMax account sign-in or BYOK with any compatible endpoint, incl. local models
- Interactive TUI, headless `mcode exec` for CI, ACP for editors
- Skills, MCP, plugins
- Plans — M Plan (Go, Explore, Build) / Token Plan

Best for:
- MiniMax M-series model users who want a first-party agent
- An MIT-licensed terminal agent that also runs other providers or local models
- Scripted / CI runs with structured output

---

## OpenAI Codex CLI

URL: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/codex/cli
Repo: https://github.com/openai/codex
License: open-source  Deployment: cli

_OpenAI's open-source (Apache 2.0) coding agent that runs locally in your terminal, with IDE extensions and the ChatGPT desktop app on the same harness._

Codex CLI is "a coding agent from OpenAI that runs locally on your
computer". The CLI is open source under Apache 2.0 and written in Rust;
the same agent is available as an IDE extension (VS Code, Cursor,
Windsurf, VS Code Insiders, with Xcode and JetBrains providing their own
integrations), inside the ChatGPT desktop app (macOS, Windows; Linux in
preview; `codex app` opens it) and as a cloud agent (Codex Cloud) at
chatgpt.com/codex.

You can sign in with a ChatGPT account — Codex in the CLI and IDE
extension is included in the Plus, Pro, Business, Edu and Enterprise
plans (Free and Go include Codex only in the ChatGPT desktop app) — or
use an API key, which OpenAI recommends for CI and shared environments.
It is not locked to OpenAI's hosted models: with `--oss` it runs against a
local "open source" provider such as Ollama or LM Studio, and custom
model providers can be defined in `config.toml`.

It supports MCP servers, lifecycle hooks, skills, AGENTS.md project
instructions and a configurable sandbox, and accepts image attachments
(`--image`).

Features:
- Terminal agent (Rust), Apache 2.0
- Sign in with ChatGPT (Plus through Enterprise) or an API key
- Local models via `--oss` (Ollama, LM Studio) and custom providers
- MCP servers, hooks, skills, AGENTS.md
- Image attachments (`--image`)
- IDE extension for VS Code-family editors; ChatGPT desktop app; Codex Cloud

Best for:
- ChatGPT subscribers who want a terminal agent included in their plan
- Open-source, auditable CLI agent with a sandbox
- Mixing hosted OpenAI models with local open-weight models

---

## OpenCode

URL: https://opencode.ai
Repo: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode
License: open-source  Deployment: cli

_MIT-licensed, provider-agnostic coding agent for the terminal (plus desktop app and IDE use) — 75+ model providers including local models._

OpenCode describes itself as "the open source AI coding agent". It is
MIT-licensed (about 211k GitHub stars as of 2026-09-29); the
repository moved from `sst/opencode` to `anomalyco/opencode`, and the
project is maintained by Anomaly.

It is provider-agnostic: the docs list support for "75+ LLM providers",
and local models through Ollama, LM Studio and llama.cpp; it can also
sign in with GitHub Copilot and ChatGPT Plus/Pro accounts. Optional paid
offerings are OpenCode Zen (pay-as-you-go access to models tested by the
OpenCode team), OpenCode Go / Go Plus (subscriptions for open models) and
an Enterprise offering. It ships two built-in agents — `build` (full
access) and `plan` (read-only, asks before running shell commands) — plus
subagents, and built-in LSP integration feeds diagnostics to the agent.

Beyond the terminal UI there is a desktop app (macOS, Windows, Linux) and
extensions for VS Code, Cursor, Zed, Windsurf and VSCodium. It supports
MCP servers, and images can be dragged into the terminal.

Features:
- Terminal agent, MIT licence
- 75+ providers; local models via Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp
- Sign in with GitHub Copilot or ChatGPT Plus/Pro accounts
- Built-in `build` and `plan` agents, subagents
- LSP integration (language-server diagnostics fed to the agent)
- MCP servers
- Image input (drag and drop)
- Desktop app (macOS, Windows, Linux) and extensions for VS Code, Cursor, Zed, Windsurf, VSCodium

Best for:
- Open-source, vendor-neutral terminal agent
- Running fully local with open-weight models
- Switching providers without switching tools

---

## Pi

URL: https://pi.dev
Repo: https://github.com/earendil-works/pi
License: open-source  Deployment: cli

_MIT-licensed minimal agent harness for the terminal (Earendil) — 15+ providers, local models, and everything else built as extensions; 1.0 shipped 2026-10-01._

Pi is "a minimal agent harness. Adapt Pi to your workflows, not the other
way around." Started by Mario Zechner and now developed by Earendil Inc.
and contributors under the MIT licence, it reached 1.0 on 2026-10-01. The
repository moved from `badlogic/pi-mono` to `earendil-works/pi` (redirects).

It deliberately ships a small core — no built-in sub-agents, plan mode,
permission popups or to-dos — and you add features as TypeScript
extensions, skills, prompt templates and themes, bundled as Pi packages
installable from npm or git. Pi 1.0 added built-in MCP with "Codemode",
reversing Pi's earlier no-MCP stance.

It supports "15+ providers, hundreds of models" (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google,
Azure, Bedrock, Mistral, Groq, xAI, OpenRouter, Ollama and more), signing in
with API keys or subscriptions via `/login`, plus local GGUF models through
the llama.cpp router and Ollama / LM Studio / vLLM via `models.json`.
Sessions are trees you can branch, export to HTML or share. Modes:
interactive TUI, print/JSON, RPC and an SDK. It installs on macOS, Linux and
Windows (PowerShell installer).

Features:
- Terminal agent, MIT; install via script (macOS / Linux / Windows) or npm
- 15+ providers; API keys or subscriptions; local models via llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM
- Extensions, skills, prompt templates, themes, shareable Pi packages
- Built-in MCP with Codemode (since 1.0)
- Branchable session trees, HTML export and sharing
- Interactive, print/JSON, RPC and SDK modes
- Image paste or drag-in

Best for:
- Developers who want a small harness they shape themselves
- Embedding an agent loop in other apps (SDK / RPC)
- Switching providers and models mid-session, including local models

---

## Qoder (incl. Qoder CLI)

URL: https://qoder.com
License: commercial  Deployment: local

_Alibaba's agentic coding platform — Qoder IDE, a JetBrains plugin and the Qoder CLI terminal agent, with Quest mode, Repo Wiki and bring-your-own-key models._

Qoder is an agentic coding platform launched by Alibaba in August 2025 and
operated by BRIGHT ZENITH PRIVATE LIMITED (Singapore). The product family
covers the Qoder IDE (Windows and macOS install guides), a JetBrains plugin,
the Qoder CLI, Cloud Agents and QoderWork.

Qoder CLI is "a command-line AI Coding Assistant under the Qoder brand". It
installs natively on macOS, Linux and Windows (arm64 / amd64; not Windows
on ARM) via a script, or via npm (`@qoder-ai/qodercli`), and runs as
`qoder`. It reads and edits files, runs shell commands, searches code and
the web, accepts images and PDFs, supports MCP, skills, plugins, subagents,
hooks, memory, ACP and headless mode, and can generate a Repo Wiki.

Individual plans are Free, Pro, Pro+ and Ultra, with Teams and Enterprise
for organisations; usage is metered in credits. Bring-your-own-key works
with preset providers (Alibaba Cloud Model Studio, DeepSeek, Z.ai, Kimi,
MiniMax, Xiaomi MiMo, OpenAI, Google, OpenRouter) and custom OpenAI- or
Anthropic-compatible endpoints; in the CLI, BYOK is available on individual
plans. The free Pro trial is not available on virtual machines.

Features:
- Qoder IDE (Editor + Quest mode), JetBrains plugin, Qoder CLI, Cloud Agents
- Qoder CLI native on macOS, Linux, Windows; headless mode for CI
- BYOK — preset providers plus OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible custom endpoints
- MCP, skills, plugins, subagents, hooks, memory, ACP
- Repo Wiki and knowledge base for codebase documentation
- Image and PDF input
- Plans — Free, Pro, Pro+, Ultra; Teams, Enterprise

Best for:
- Long-running delegated tasks (Quest mode, goal mode)
- Teams standardising on Qwen and other Chinese model providers
- Generating repository documentation (Repo Wiki)

---

## Qwen Code

URL: https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/
Repo: https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code
License: open-source  Deployment: cli

_Alibaba's Apache-2.0 coding agent for terminal, editor and desktop — multi-protocol, with any third-party provider or local model._

Qwen Code is "the open-source AI coding agent for your terminal, editor,
desktop, browser, and chat", from Alibaba's Qwen team, licensed
Apache 2.0. It is developed alongside the Qwen models but is
multi-protocol: it
"Supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and Qwen APIs. Any third-party
provider or local model (Ollama / vLLM)."

It ships subagents, agent teams, auto-memory, skills and MCP. Editor
integrations are a VS Code companion extension (beta), Zed and JetBrains;
there is also a desktop app (macOS, Windows, Linux), web UI, SDKs and
chat integrations.

The Qwen OAuth free tier was discontinued on 2026-04-15; the recommended
setup is Alibaba ModelStudio (Coding Plan / Token Plan / API key).

Features:
- Terminal agent, Apache 2.0
- OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and Qwen API protocols; local models via Ollama / vLLM
- Subagents, agent teams, auto-memory, skills
- MCP support
- VS Code (beta), Zed and JetBrains integrations; desktop app

Best for:
- Qwen-model users who want a first-party agent
- Open-source agent with local-model support
- Teams mixing Chinese and Western model providers

## Sourcegraph Cody (Enterprise only)

URL: https://sourcegraph.com/docs/cody
License: commercial  Deployment: local

_Sourcegraph's code-search-backed coding assistant — now sold only as part of Sourcegraph Enterprise; Cody Free and Pro were discontinued in July 2025._

Cody pairs an AI assistant with Sourcegraph's code search and code graph,
which is why it is aimed at very large codebases and monorepos. Its docs
describe it as "Supported on Sourcegraph Enterprise", available in VS Code,
JetBrains, Visual Studio and the web app, plus a Cody CLI.

Individual plans are gone: Sourcegraph stopped Cody Free and Cody Pro
signups on 2025-06-25 and cut off access on 2025-07-23, while stating that
"Cody Enterprise customers are not affected by these changes." The client
is no longer developed in the open: the public source now lives in
`sourcegraph/cody-public-snapshot`, archived since 2025-08-01.

Sourcegraph's newer agent, Amp, spun out as an independent company in
December 2025 (see Amp); Sourcegraph itself now focuses on code search.
